intro: Variable-length sequences need a rectangular batch, but the padding value alone cannot tell you which positions were originally present.
task: Right-pad a batch of token-ID lists to the longest sequence and return both tokens and a boolean presence mask.
requirements: sequences is a nonempty list of lists of nonnegative integer values. Empty sequences are allowed. pad_id is a nonnegative integer excluding booleans.
Return tokens and mask as NumPy arrays with shape (batch, longest_length). mask is boolean and True for original positions.
A real token may equal pad_id; determine the mask from lengths. An all-empty batch has arrays of shape (batch,0).
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Find the maximum input length, fill the token matrix with pad_id, and initialize a false mask.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Copy each sequence into its prefix and mark that prefix true.

explanation: Padding makes sequence shapes compatible for batch operations. The presence mask records which entries have semantic content and which exist only to fill the rectangle.
Comparing token values with the padding identifier is insufficient when that identifier can also occur in real input. Length information preserves the distinction.
Use zero as both a real token and the padding value. Trace which positions a loss function should include and explain the error caused by masking every zero.
